title: How to pause notifications in Slack on Mac: profile menu, schedules and /dnd for 2026
metaTitle: How to Pause Notifications in Slack on Mac (2026 Guide)
description: Learn how to pause notifications in Slack on Mac from the profile menu, plus the /dnd command, schedules, resume steps and common fixes.
targetKeyword: how to pause notifications in slack on mac
intro: In Slack on Mac, click your profile picture in the sidebar and hover over Notifications. Then pick a time frame, or choose Custom to set your own end time.
tldr: Click your profile picture, hover over Notifications, and pick a time frame or Custom.
Type /dnd for 15 mins or /dnd until 17:00 for a quick pause.
Set a repeating quiet period under Preferences > Working hours > Allow notifications.
Resume from the same Notifications menu with Resume notifications, or type /dnd off.
Control Center Do Not Disturb is a separate macOS switch. Check it if banners still go missing.

blocks.text: What a Slack pause does and does not do

A Slack pause stops Slack from interrupting you with alerts. Messages still reach your workspace while the pause runs. You decide when to look at them, and Slack keeps them where they are so you can catch up later.

Two other controls get mixed up with a Slack pause. One is Do Not Disturb in Control Center, which is a macOS setting. The other is Shift Esc, which marks everything as read. Shift Esc is not a pause at all, so skip it when you want quiet.
Pause notifications from the profile menu

This is the fastest way to stop alerts for a set time. You use your profile picture in the sidebar, then the Notifications item. The menu gives you time frames, plus a Custom option when none of them fit.
Once a pause is active, Slack shows a snooze icon next to your name. Other people see that icon too. It tells them you are not getting alerts right now, so they know to expect a slower reply.
Choose a time frame or a custom end time

Slack's official article says to pick a time frame from the menu, or select Custom. It does not list the durations. So the labels on your screen are the only guide to what each option does. Read them before you click, and check for the snooze icon afterward.

A quick break without the mouse
Quiet hours every day or on weekdays
blocks.caption: Five ways to pause Slack, from quickest to most repeatable.

blocks.text: Custom suits a pause that must end at a set time. Use it when you have a block of focus work with a known end. If the end time is wrong, open the same menu and choose Resume notifications. You do not have to wait for the timer.
Use the /dnd slash command for quick pauses
Slash commands are typed rather than clicked. They help when your hands are already on the keyboard. Slack's help article lists the commands below, and it covers the desktop app and the web app.

items: /dnd for 15 mins or /dnd 15 minutes pauses for that length of time.
/dnd until 17:00 or /dnd until 5pm pauses until a clock time.
/dnd until tonight or /dnd until tomorrow morning pauses until that point.

blocks.text: After you run a command, check for the snooze icon next to your name. That icon confirms the pause took. Use /dnd off when you want alerts back early, the same way you would use Resume notifications in the menu.
Set a daily or weekday notification schedule

A schedule is different from a pause. A pause is a one-off stop that you start yourself. A schedule repeats, so Slack quiets alerts each day without another click. Slack's help article says that outside the schedule you set, your notifications are paused.

Choose Every day if your hours stay the same across the week. Choose Weekdays if you only want Slack alerts from Monday to Friday. Choose Custom when your week follows its own pattern, and set the start and end times yourself.

blocks.title: Admin defaults
blocks.text: An owner or admin can set a default schedule for your workspace. Your own schedule overrides that default. If the default does not suit you, set your own schedule in Preferences.
Schedules keep working even when you forget about them. That is the point. Look at your schedule once a month, or when your hours change, so alerts do not stay quiet by accident.
Resume notifications early

Ending a pause early takes one trip through the same menu. A manual pause and a schedule are separate settings. If you resume during scheduled quiet hours, check the schedule before you assume alerts are back. The schedule still pauses notifications outside its hours.

The mobile app uses different labels. Slack's article lists Pause notifications and Notification schedule for phones. This page covers the Mac app only, so do not expect those exact words in the Mac menu.
What still gets through during a pause

A pause is not a total wall. Slack lets a sender override it once per day to notify you about an urgent direct message. One urgent DM can still reach you during a pause, so plan for that on a busy day.

items: Urgent direct messages: a sender can override the pause once per day.
VIP list members: they can still reach you during a pause.
Everyone else: they see a snooze icon next to your name.

blocks.text: The VIP list is the setting to check before you pause. Slack's notification settings article explains how the list works. Look at it if a manager, a client, or a team lead must always reach you. This guide does not cover adding people to the list.
Slack pause versus Mac Do Not Disturb

macOS has its own Do Not Disturb switch in Control Center. You open Control Center from the icon at the top right of the menu bar. When Do Not Disturb is on, Slack banners can go missing even if Slack is not paused. Slack's troubleshooting article tells you to make sure it is off.

blocks.text: Use the table as a checklist. If a banner is missing, check Control Center first. Then check the Slack pause and the schedule. Last, check the macOS permission for Slack under System Settings > Notifications. Work down the list so you change one thing at a time.
Why pausing Slack matters: the numbers

Slack's own research shows how much work leaks past standard hours. The survey covered 10,333 workers in the U.S., Australia, France, Germany, Japan, and the U.K. It ran from August 24 to September 15, 2023. In that survey, 37% of desk workers logged on outside standard hours at least weekly.

Microsoft's 2025 Work Trend Index describes a similar pattern. It says employees are interrupted every 2 minutes by meetings, emails, or pings. The survey covered 31,000 knowledge workers across 31 markets, fielded from February 6 to March 24, 2025.

Treat the two-minute figure as a rough guide. Microsoft's report gives 275 interruptions a day, but it describes that count two ways, once for a 24-hour day and once for core work hours. A pause will not stop meetings or email. It only quiets Slack, so count how often Slack pulls you away on a normal day.
Keyboard shortcuts for Slack on Mac

Slack's keyboard navigation article covers the desktop app and the browser. It lists no shortcut for pausing notifications or Do Not Disturb. It also lists no shortcut for Preferences. So the menu and the slash commands are the documented ways to pause.

items: ⌘ K opens a channel or direct message through search.
⌘ J moves focus to the first unread message.

blocks.text: Shift Esc deserves a warning. Slack's troubleshooting article uses it to clear stuck badges by marking everything as read. People mix it up with a pause. It is not one, and it changes your unread state for every channel.
Catch up after you resume

When you resume, start with the messages that matter. Press ⌘ J to jump to the first unread message. Open the Unreads view if you want a list. Mark all messages as read only when you are sure nothing is left to answer. For the full steps, read [how to view unread messages in Slack on Mac](/how-to/view-all-unread-messages-in-slack) and [how to mark all messages as read in Slack on Mac](/how-to/mark-all-messages-as-read-in-slack).
Check your Slack version and release notes

Slack's help pages do not list version numbers. So the steps on this page are not tied to one build. The Mac release notes list recent builds, such as 4.53.280 from November 3, 2026. Those notes do not mention pause, snooze, or menu changes.

That is weak evidence, since the notes are mostly security and bug-fix text. If a label on your screen differs from this page, trust the screen. Then check [Preferences in Slack on Mac](/how-to/open-preferences-in-slack) for the current location of the settings you need.
Mistakes people make when pausing Slack

items: Treating Control Center's Do Not Disturb as the Slack pause.
Pressing Shift Esc to pause, which only marks items as read.
Forgetting that a schedule keeps running after you resume a manual pause.
Setting a pause and never checking for the snooze icon, so you do not know it took.
Skipping the VIP list when a manager or client must reach you.

blocks.text: Most of these come from mixing up two controls. Check the Slack pause, the schedule, and the Mac setting in that order. Working through them in order usually shows the cause fast.

faq.question: Does pausing Slack on my Mac also pause it on my phone?
faq.answer: Slack's help article gives separate steps for mobile, with different labels such as Pause notifications and Notification schedule. Check the phone app separately. This page covers the desktop steps that Slack documents.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to pause Slack notifications on Mac?
faq.answer: Not one that Slack documents. Its pause article and its keyboard navigation article list no shortcut for pausing or Do Not Disturb. Use the profile menu, or type /dnd in a message box. Shift Esc is not a pause, because it marks items as read.

faq.question: Can people tell that I paused notifications?
faq.answer: Yes, in one way. Others see a snooze icon next to your name while the pause runs. A sender can still override the pause once per day for an urgent direct message.

faq.question: Why do I still see a snooze icon after I resumed?
faq.answer: A snooze icon means a pause is active. Open the profile picture menu, hover over Notifications, and check the state. Also check your Working hours schedule, because Slack pauses notifications outside those hours.

faq.question: Why are Slack banners missing when I have not paused Slack?
faq.answer: Check Control Center first. If Do Not Disturb is on, Mac banners stay hidden. Then open System Settings > Notifications > Slack and make sure Allow Notifications from Slack is on.

faq.question: Does an admin control my notification schedule?
faq.answer: An owner or admin can set a default schedule for the workspace. Slack's help article says your own schedule overrides that default. So the settings in your own Preferences are the ones that apply to you.

faq.question: Which Slack version do I need for these steps?
faq.answer: Slack's help pages state no version numbers, so the steps are not tied to one build. Recent Mac release notes mention no pause or snooze changes. If your menu looks different, trust what you see on screen.

faq.question: What does /dnd for 15 mins do exactly?
faq.answer: It pauses notifications for 15 minutes, according to Slack's help article. Then alerts come back on their own. Use /dnd off to resume early. The article lists no other durations, so use Custom in the menu for other lengths.

steps.name: Open Slack on your Mac
steps.text: Open the Slack desktop app. Slack's help article gives one set of steps that covers the Mac app, the Windows app, and the web app, so the steps below apply to all three.

steps.name: Click your profile picture
steps.text: Find your profile picture in the sidebar and click it. A menu opens. Slack's help article starts the pause from this menu, so start here.

steps.name: Hover over Notifications
steps.text: Move the pointer over Notifications in the menu. A second list of pause options opens next to it.

steps.name: Pick a time frame
steps.text: Choose one of the time frames in the list. Slack's help article does not list the durations, so read the labels on your screen before you pick one.
steps.tip: The help article does not list the durations, so the labels on your screen are the only check.

steps.name: Or choose Custom
steps.text: Select Custom if none of the time frames fit. Set your own end time in the dialog that opens. The help article does not list the dialog fields, so follow the labels on screen.

steps.name: Check for the snooze icon
steps.text: Look for a snooze icon next to your name. It means your notifications are paused in Slack. Other people see the same icon, so it also tells them to expect a slower reply.

steps.name: Resume notifications early
steps.text: To end the pause, click your profile picture, hover over Notifications, and select Resume notifications. Alerts return as soon as the pause ends.

steps.name: Set a recurring schedule
steps.text: Open Preferences from the profile picture menu. Under Working hours, open the Allow notifications drop-down and pick Every day, Weekdays, or Custom. For Custom, choose the start and end times. Slack saves the settings automatically.
steps.tip: Slack's help article lists no keyboard shortcut for Preferences, so use the menu.

steps.name: Type a quick /dnd command
steps.text: In a message box, type /dnd for 15 mins to pause for 15 minutes, or /dnd until 17:00 to pause until 5 p.m. Type /dnd off to resume early.

steps.name: Confirm the pause took
steps.text: After any pause, check the snooze icon next to your name. If it is missing, open the menu again and confirm the time frame or command you chose.

troubleshooting.problem: Banners still show during a pause
troubleshooting.fix: Open Control Center from the top-right icon in the menu bar, click Do Not Disturb, and make sure it is off. A snooze icon next to your name confirms that Slack is paused.

troubleshooting.problem: Slack alerts are missing when Slack is not paused
troubleshooting.fix: Open System Settings > Notifications > Slack. Turn on Allow Notifications from Slack, set the alert style to Banners or Alerts, and keep the option for when mirroring or sharing the display enabled.
On macOS 12 Monterey or later, turn on Play sound for notifications under System Settings > Notifications > Slack. In Slack, open Preferences > Sounds & appearance and click Show an example.

troubleshooting.problem: Browser notifications from the Slack web app are blocked
troubleshooting.fix: In Chrome, go to Preferences > Privacy and security > Site Settings > Permissions > Notifications and turn on Sites can ask to send notifications. In Safari, go to Safari > Preferences > Websites > Notifications and make sure the workspace is allowed.

troubleshooting.problem: An unread badge will not clear
troubleshooting.fix: Press Shift Esc to mark everything as read. This clears the badge. It does not pause notifications, so use the profile menu for that.

troubleshooting.problem: The problem continues after these checks
troubleshooting.fix: Click Help in the menu bar, then Troubleshooting > Report Issue. Add a short summary and click Send us a message so Slack can review the logs.
